h1: What building code rules apply to building an ADU in a basement in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Basement ADU Requirements: Egress, Ceiling Height and Safety
description: Understand the state definition of an ADU and why a basement unit must also meet applicable building and life-safety codes.
short_answer: A basement ADU must qualify as a self-contained dwelling unit with sleeping, cooking, and sanitary facilities and a separate entrance that meets safe-egress requirements. Massachusetts ADU regulations do not replace the state building code or fire-safety rules. The exact ceiling height, emergency escape opening, and fire-separation requirements must be confirmed for the proposed basement design.

facts.text: Massachusetts defines an ADU as a self-contained housing unit with sleeping, cooking, and sanitary facilities on the same lot as the principal dwelling, with a separate entrance.
The state ADU regulation states that it is not intended to supersede the Building Code, Fire Code, Lead Law, or other state and federal health and safety laws.

qa.q: Does the ADU law waive basement egress or ceiling-height rules?
qa.a: No. The ADU regulation does not supersede the state Building Code or Fire Code. The proposed basement unit must meet the applicable building and life-safety requirements.
